objective.jobToBeDone: Create, edit, and approve or reject change orders so that cost and schedule impacts are accurately recorded against the active project.
objective.primaryDecision: Approve or reject a change order after reviewing its cost and schedule impact — the status transition is the highest-stakes action on this page.
objective.usageFrequency: Occasional / back-office — triggered when a project scope change arises; not a high-frequency POS-style interaction.

criticalActions.presentation: contextual-transition-actions — render Approve and Reject as explicit buttons on the selected change order; Reject conditionally reveals a rejection-reason input; never a free <select>.
primary-button opening an inline form panel; projectId is context-derived (hidden), never typed.
inline-row-command / edit panel pre-populated from the selected change order; changeOrderId is route-derived (hidden).

informationHierarchy: 1. Change order list with current status badges — lets the PM scan what needs attention
2. Detail / edit panel for the selected change order (title, description, impactType, costAdjustment, scheduleAdjustmentDays)
3. Status transition actions (Approve / Reject) with rejection-reason field shown conditionally
4. Create new change order form (secondary, triggered by explicit action)
objective.successCriteria: The PM can review all change orders for a project at a glance, open one to inspect or edit its details, and approve or reject it in two clicks — without ever typing an id or selecting a status from a dropdown.
antiPatterns: Free <select> over all status enum values for status transitions
Manually typed changeOrderId or projectId inputs
Separate full-page form for status update
Stacking three independent form sections without a master-detail relationship
Showing system-owned fields (createdAt, updatedAt, approvedAt, rejectedAt) as editable inputs
